beginner.headline: Zelensky Backs Energy Ceasefire Amid Continued Attacks
beginner.brief: President Zelensky supports an 'energy ceasefire'. Ukraine's leader says he will support such a truce if Moscow does. Donald Trump said Russia and Ukraine agreed to this 'energy ceasefire'. But President Zelensky said Russia continued to hit power plants. Russia attacked Ukrainian energy places after Trump's announcement. For many months, Ukraine and Russia have attacked each other's energy buildings. These attacks caused problems with energy for both sides. Russia said its attacks were fair because these places helped Ukraine's army.

intermediate.headline: Zelensky's Conditional Support for Energy Ceasefire Amid New Strikes
intermediate.brief: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated he would support an "energy ceasefire" if Russia also agreed. He initially expressed surprise at Donald Trump's announcement of this ceasefire. Donald Trump claimed that Russia and Ukraine had already agreed to an "energy ceasefire," though Moscow has yet to comment. However, Zelensky later accused Russia of striking Ukrainian energy facilities after Trump's announcement. Trump has been urging Ukraine to stop strikes on Russian oil infrastructure. He wants Russia to fulfill a deal to release diesel to the global market. This diesel deal, which temporarily undoes sanctions on Russian imports, is attracting significant criticism. Zelensky himself called it "a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin." Some European officials and US politicians also stated they do not support the deal. Trump suggested that it was "time for Ukraine to get a new president." For many months, Ukraine and Russia have been exchanging strikes on each other's energy infrastructure.

advanced.headline: Zelensky Conditionally Backs 'Energy Ceasefire' Amid Russian Strikes
advanced.brief: Volodymyr Zelensky has expressed conditional support for a proposed 'energy ceasefire' between Ukraine and Russia, which Donald Trump claimed was already in effect. Trump had insisted that the truce was 'effective immediately' but did not provide any specific details. Zelensky initially expressed surprise at the announcement, then confirmed Kyiv would back the measure if Moscow also agreed. However, Ukraine's President also accused Russia of striking Ukrainian energy facilities after Trump's public post. Trump has been advocating for Ukraine to halt its strikes on Russian oil infrastructure, arguing this would allow Russia to release diesel to the US and global market. This controversial diesel deal, which temporarily lifts sanctions on Russian imports, has drawn increasing condemnation. Zelensky explicitly called the agreement a 'gift' to Russian President Vladimir Putin, a sentiment echoed by European officials and some US politicians. Trump's latest initiative aims to lower domestic fuel prices before the midterm elections, following months of political backlash from a separate conflict. The higher pump prices and subsequent knock-on effects have soured Trump's standing with the American public, contributing to widespread inflation. Ukraine and Russia have engaged in months of retaliatory strikes targeting each other's energy infrastructure. Moscow asserts these installations are legitimate targets supporting Ukraine's military operations, while Kyiv views its attacks as essential to curtailing Russia's war finance capabilities. These sustained attacks have consequently disrupted energy supplies across both nations. Seven senators from both major US parties have issued a statement declaring Trump's deal 'runs directly counter' to a law prohibiting Russian energy imports. They urged the Trump administration to 'reverse course', emphasizing that Congress's intention was clear: no Russian oil imports until aggression against Ukraine ceases. Republican Senator Thom Tillis stated that the deal 'absolutely will' endanger American lives.
